headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action hazards; Semantic Kernel’s MCP/plugin model amplifies the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra writes to shared files and processes workflow inputs/logs, while Semantic Kernel can use MCP servers and plugins. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if Kestra outputs are fed into SK prompts or tools. The path is not proven by docs, so I choose medium rather than low because the shared-file and tool-bridge surfaces are explicit.
conditions: IF Kestra outputs are passed into Semantic Kernel prompts or plugin inputs
IF an MCP server or plugin reads Kestra-generated files without provenance filtering
mitigations: Add a strict allowlist for files passed from Kestra to Semantic Kernel
Strip instructions from workflow outputs before prompting SK
Disable MCP plugins for untrusted content paths
Tag Kestra artifacts with provenance metadata
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance checks

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, and has broad network egress. Semantic Kernel handles secrets and can call external model providers and MCP servers. If Kestra data is forwarded into SK, the pair can exfiltrate sensitive operational data to third parties by default, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Kestra workflows pass logs, database data, or cloud-storage data into Semantic Kernel
IF Semantic Kernel routes that context to Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Hugging Face, or MCP servers
mitigations: Restrict SK inputs to redacted summaries
Block sensitive Kestra artifacts from model-provider calls
Use separate credentials for orchestration and model access
Turn off broad egress on the Kestra host where feasible
requires-engineering: add DLP and egress policy enforcement

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra has filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and elevated-privilege requests; Semantic Kernel has filesystem write and shared-state via memory store. Even without git writes, both can mutate shared resources concurrently, and the orchestrator does not advertise locking. That makes write conflicts and state corruption likely in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory, memory store, or artifact path
IF multiple instances run without external locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint working directories
Serialize writes with a lock file or queue
Separate memory-store namespaces per agent
Avoid shared mutable state for artifacts
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can emit workflow outputs, notifications, and API actions, while Semantic Kernel is an agent framework that can consume those outputs through plugins or MCP. If SK treats Kestra-produced facts as authoritative, errors can cascade into emails, cloud actions, or other downstream operations. The default interaction is risky enough to rate high.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel uses Kestra outputs as tool inputs without verification
IF downstream plugins send notifications or execute actions based on those outputs
mitigations: Require human review before action-taking plugins run
Add schema validation to Kestra outputs
Cross-check critical facts against a second source
Disable auto-execution for high-impact workflows
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra processes database, cloud-storage, messages, and notifications, while Semantic Kernel handles model-provider keys and plugin credentials and can send data to external APIs. The profiles do not state residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. I choose medium because the data classes are broad and the uncertainty should escalate.
conditions: IF regulated data from Kestra is sent through Semantic Kernel to external model providers
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared data class
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of SK prompts
Document data-flow and residency boundaries
Set shorter retention on shared logs and artifacts
Use region-pinned model endpoints where available
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
